xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2609: Session Vault: versioned, encrypted, off-machine storage and cross-machine resume for agent conversations

plan.title: Session Vault: versioned, encrypted, off-machine storage and cross-machine resume for agent conversations
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: PAN-2609 creates one new module directory (src/lib/vault/, about 17 small single-purpose files, each with its own test) plus its standalone CLI group (src/cli/commands/vault/) and five doc files. The projected-surface lint counts each test and doc path separately, and each docs/ or configuration/ file as its own subsystem, so the new-module surface alone exceeds 25 files and 6 subsystems. The separable consumers were already split out as siblings PAN-4307 (dashboard) and PAN-4308 (Fly); what remains is inseparable because the CLI verbs are the only way to exercise and accept the engine, and the issue-level acceptance criteria are defined through them.

narratives.Problem: Agent transcripts, conversation rows and live panes live only on the machine that created them. Work started on one machine is invisible on another, nothing can move transcripts off the machine (about 30 GB on the operator machine), only Claude Code can resume natively, and there is no way to version, back up and resume agent sessions without adopting the whole orchestrator.
narratives.Proposal: Build the Session Vault engine in src/lib/vault/: an always-encrypted (AES-256-GCM, client-held key with a 24-word recovery phrase), content-addressed chunk + LOG + VIEW record format with a continuity check, secret scan and cwd-state summary on every settlement; a VaultStore interface with git (v1) and dir (tests) backends using compare-and-swap refs; single-owner records with CAS adoption; operator-confirmed eviction batches through one leaf deletion door. Expose it as a standalone pan vault CLI (setup, join, status, save, sync, list, show, resume, evict, restore, exclude, include, allow-secret, setup --hooks) that works with no dashboard and no pan install and sends no telemetry. Reuse PAN-3762 environmentId as the machine identity, creating environment-identity.ts in the shared-contract form. Dashboard surfaces go to PAN-4307 and Fly settlement to PAN-4308.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No dashboard UI, dashboard routes, vault-service.ts, browse rows in overdeck.db, or dashboard sync timer (PAN-4307)
- No Fly remote reap integration (PAN-4308)
- No hosted overdeck.ai backend or overdeck:// URL scheme (PAN-4297)
- No automatic deletion of any native transcript: no timer, sync cycle, retention policy, config value or hook deletes one; only confirmEviction does
- No change to the CLAUDE.md "JSONL session files are sacred" line
- No separate machineId and no machine-id.json file
- No writes to ~/.overdeck/config.yaml, src/lib/config-yaml/**, or the dashboard settings schema for vault keys
- No writes to any Codex state_*.sqlite file
- No git stash, and no git operation on any repository other than the vault clone
- No telemetry, analytics or heartbeat from pan vault verbs
- No new npm dependency and no native addon
- No purge or garbage collection of tombstoned or unreferenced chunks from backend history
- No real-time co-editing (CRDT) of one live session and no sharing with other people
- No model call anywhere in the vault, including the seeded fallback

autoDecisions.summary: Split the dashboard consumer into PAN-4307 and Fly settlement into PAN-4308; PAN-2609 keeps the engine, standalone CLI and docs
autoDecisions.rationale: Every issue-level acceptance criterion is satisfiable through the pan vault CLI, the PRD calls the dashboard one consumer, and the swarm contract prefers sibling issues over one mega-plan; Fly settlement also depends on still-open PAN-4295

autoDecisions.summary: AC-4 'within one sync interval' means after pan vault sync on A then on B
autoDecisions.rationale: Standalone mode has no daemon; the periodic timer belongs to the dashboard sibling

autoDecisions.summary: Vault config lives in ${OVERDECK_HOME}/vault/config.json via src/lib/vault/config.ts, not config.yaml (P-1)
autoDecisions.rationale: The config-yaml loader pulls in the whole settings schema, which conflicts with the NFR-7 standalone footprint

autoDecisions.summary: The recovery phrase is the BIP-39 entropy encoding of the key with a vendored wordlist; no scrypt, no new dependency (P-2)
autoDecisions.rationale: A 256-bit random key needs no stretching, and NFR-9 bans new dependencies for crypto

autoDecisions.summary: Git backend never keeps a local commit after a failed push; casRef resets to origin/main (P-4)
autoDecisions.rationale: Removes divergent local history and rebase conflicts while keeping CAS semantics; the vault clone is not a project repo

autoDecisions.summary: Adoption adds an owner segment to the same record; an owner that lost the record while offline saves its new lines as a fork (P-5, P-6)
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps settlement continuity checkable on the adopter file and never discards data (FR-8)

autoDecisions.summary: Secret scan blocks only on API key, token, AWS, JWT, database URL, basic-auth URL and private key; env assignments and labelled secrets stay redaction-only (P-8)
autoDecisions.rationale: FOO=bar and token: x appear in almost every coding transcript; blocking them would refuse most sessions

autoDecisions.summary: Extract the deletion door into the leaf transcript-deletion-door.ts shared with transcript-retention.ts (P-9)
autoDecisions.rationale: transcript-retention.ts imports SQLite and terminal-backend modules at top, which breaks the standalone CLI; one door stays one door

autoDecisions.summary: Standalone liveness = transcript mtime older than liveQuietMinutes (default 30) (P-10)
autoDecisions.rationale: No backend inventory exists without the dashboard; PAN-4307 adds the liveness.ts check

autoDecisions.summary: pan vault bypasses CLI telemetry and heartbeat (P-12)
autoDecisions.rationale: NFR-8 and the issue promise no telemetry, while the CLI sends anonymous PostHog events by default

autoDecisions.summary: Codex resume: test native rollout placement; else deterministic seeded fallback; never write Codex SQLite (P-16)
autoDecisions.rationale: The threads table schema has grown about 25 columns across versions (checked on codex-cli 0.158.0), so row insertion is fragile

autoDecisions.summary: The seeded fallback is a deterministic digest with no model call
autoDecisions.rationale: Standalone mode has no configured summarizer, NFR-8 forbids non-backend network calls, and repo rules forbid a hardcoded model fallback

items.title: Create the shared machine identity module environment-identity.ts

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/environment-identity.ts exactly per the PRD section "Shared machine identity contract": readEnvironmentIdentity() and ensureEnvironmentIdentity() over ${OVERDECK_HOME}/environment-id.json (mode 0600, temp file + rename, created only when absent, shape { v: 1, environmentId: lowercase UUID v4, label: os.hostname(), createdAt: ISO UTC }). Import only Node built-ins and src/lib/paths.ts. A corrupt or unparseable file makes both functions throw an Error whose message names the file path; never re-mint. Never write machine-id.json. PAN-3762 W1 adopts this module unchanged, so do not add fields.

items.title: Given an empty OVERDECK_HOME, when ensureEnvironmentIdentity() runs twice, then it creates environment-id.json once with mode 0600 and returns the same environmentId both times
Given two different OVERDECK_HOME temp dirs, when ensureEnvironmentIdentity() runs in each, then it returns two different UUID v4 values
Given environment-id.json contains invalid JSON, when readEnvironmentIdentity() runs, then it throws an error that names the file path and the file is left unchanged
Given any run of the test suite, then no file named machine-id.json exists under OVERDECK_HOME
Add the vault config file module config.ts with isVaultEnabled

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/config.ts per PRD decision P-1: vaultDir() = ${OVERDECK_HOME}/vault, readVaultConfig()/writeVaultConfig() over vault/config.json (mode 0600, atomic temp+rename), defaults backend absent, exclude {paths:[],origins:[],sessions:[]}, syncIntervalSec 300, debounceSec 30, evict false, liveQuietMinutes 30, maxChunkBytes 67108864, and isVaultEnabled() false when backend is absent. Export the constant VAULT_OFF_MESSAGE = "Session Vault is off. Run: pan vault setup <git-url>". Do not touch ~/.overdeck/config.yaml or src/lib/config-yaml/**.

items.title: Given no vault/config.json, when readVaultConfig() runs, then it returns every P-1 default and isVaultEnabled() returns false
Given writeVaultConfig({ backend: "file:///x" }), when the file is read back, then it persists with mode 0600 and isVaultEnabled() returns true
Given a config file missing some keys, when readVaultConfig() runs, then it falls back to the P-1 default for each missing key
Generate the vault key and encode it as a 24-word recovery phrase

narrative.Action: Implement src/lib/vault/identity.ts per PRD "Encryption (D-3)" and decision P-2: createVaultKey() (32 random bytes via node:crypto), saveVaultKey/loadVaultKey at vaultDir()/key (mode 0600, raw bytes), keyToPhrase/phraseToKey as the BIP-39 entropy encoding (256 bits + 8-bit SHA-256 checksum, 24 words), and deriveSubkeys(K) returning K_enc, K_id, K_ref via HKDF-SHA256 with info strings "overdeck-vault enc", "overdeck-vault id", "overdeck-vault ref". Vendor the English wordlist in bip39-english.ts as one space-separated string with the source URL comment. No new dependency; node:crypto only.

items.title: Given 32 zero bytes, when keyToPhrase runs, then it returns "abandon" 23 times followed by "art"
Given 32 bytes of 0x7f, when keyToPhrase runs, then it returns "legal winner thank year wave sausage worth useful" three times with the last word replaced by "title"
Given a random key, when phraseToKey(keyToPhrase(key)) runs, then it returns the identical 32 bytes
Given a phrase with one word changed or an unknown word, when phraseToKey runs, then it rejects with a message naming the word position
Given saveVaultKey runs, then the key file persists with mode 0600
Implement line hashing and the noop/append/diverged continuity check

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/continuity.ts: lineHash(line) = first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of the raw line bytes; splitSettleableLines(buffer) that splits on \n and drops a trailing line that is not complete JSON; and checkContinuity(tail, liveLines) where tail = { lineCount, byteOffset, lastHashes (up to 16) } returns "noop" when the live file has no lines past lineCount, "append" when the live hashes at positions lineCount-16..lineCount-1 equal lastHashes, else "diverged". Export the Tail type; vault-format and vault-settle import it.

items.title: Given a live file that equals the saved lines, when checkContinuity runs, then it returns "noop"
Given a live file that only grew, when checkContinuity runs, then it returns "append" with the new lines
Given a live file with one middle line changed inside the last 16 saved lines, when checkContinuity runs, then it returns "diverged"
Given a file whose last line is incomplete JSON, when splitSettleableLines runs, then it drops that line and a later call that sees the completed line returns it
Define the encrypted chunk and record wire format format.ts

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns only its new file format.ts and its test; its inputs (continuity.ts lineHash, identity.ts subkeys) arrive through blocks edges.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/format.ts per PRD "Record format", "Encryption (D-3)", decisions P-3, P-5, P-7, P-19: encodeChunk(lines, keys) builds the plaintext { v:1, codec:"zstd", lineHashes, lines } (lines are raw bytes as strings, never re-serialized), chunkId = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_id, plaintext))[:40], compresses with promisified zlib.zstdCompress, encrypts AES-256-GCM with a random 96-bit nonce and the chunk id as associated data, stored as nonce||ciphertext||tag; decodeChunk reverses it and rejects any auth failure. splitIntoChunks(lines, maxChunkBytes) implements NFR-6. encryptRef/decryptRef do the same for record, machine and header ref values. Define the SessionRecord type (fields from "Record format" plus type: "session", segments per P-5, parent {vaultId, version} per P-7) and refName(kind, id, K_ref) producing r/, m/, h/header names. Readers return null for a decrypted value whose type is not "session" (FR-9 reservation).

items.title: Given lines with arbitrary bytes, when encodeChunk then decodeChunk run, then the decoded lines are byte-identical to the input
Given an encoded chunk with one flipped byte, when decodeChunk runs, then it rejects with an authentication error
Given two chunks, when chunk A bytes are decoded under chunk B id, then decodeChunk rejects (associated data binds the id)
Given lines totalling more than maxChunkBytes, when splitIntoChunks runs, then it produces several chunks each under the limit and their concatenation equals the input
Given an encrypted ref value with type "task", when the record reader runs, then it returns null without throwing
Count human turns with the known injected-prefix filter turns.ts

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/turns.ts: isHumanTurn(line, harness) and countHumanTurns(lines, harness) per FR-18. A Claude Code user line is not a human turn when its text starts with <task-notification>, <command-name>, <local-command-stdout>, <local-command-caveat>, or [Request interrupted by user], or when isCompactSummary is true or it carries tool_result content. A Codex user line is not a human turn when it starts with <environment_context>, <codex_internal_context>, or # Files mentioned by the user:. Match by these exact prefixes, never by "starts with <".

items.title: Given a Claude fixture with 3 typed prompts and 4 injected lines of the listed kinds, when countHumanTurns runs, then it returns 3
Given a Codex fixture with 2 typed prompts and an <environment_context> line, when countHumanTurns runs, then it returns 2
Given a typed prompt that starts with "<div>", when isHumanTurn runs, then it returns true
Export findSecretMatches from secret-redaction.ts with the blocking pattern set

narrative.Action: Per PRD decision P-8: first add tests/unit/lib/secret-redaction.test.ts pinning redactSensitiveText output for one sample of every existing pattern. Then add export type SecretPatternName = "api-key" | "token" | "aws-access-key" | "jwt" | "database-url" | "basic-auth-url" | "private-key" and export function findSecretMatches(text) returning { pattern, start, end } for matches of API_KEY_PATTERN, TOKEN_PATTERN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_PATTERN, JWT_PATTERN, DATABASE_URL_PATTERN, BASIC_AUTH_URL_PATTERN and the private-key scan, reusing the existing constants and collectors. ENV_ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN and LABELLED_SECRET_PATTERN are not part of findSecretMatches.

items.title: Given the pinned samples, when redactSensitiveText runs after the change, then it returns the same strings as before the change
Given text containing a GitHub token and an AWS key, when findSecretMatches runs, then it returns two matches named "token" and "aws-access-key" with their offsets
Given the line "export FOO=bar token: abc", when findSecretMatches runs, then it returns no matches
Block settlement on secret hits with per-line allow list secrets.ts

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/secrets.ts per FR-13 and P-8: scanNewLines(vaultId, lines, firstLineNumber) calls findSecretMatches per line, skips lines whose lineHash is allowed for that vaultId in vaultDir()/allowed-secrets.json (0600), and returns hits as { line, pattern } without the matched value. allowSecret(vaultId, lineHash) persists an allow entry.

items.title: Given a line containing an API key, when scanNewLines runs, then it returns a hit naming the line number and "api-key" and the returned object contains no substring of the key
Given allowSecret was called for that line hash and vaultId, when scanNewLines runs again, then it returns no hit for that line
Given the allow entry is for a different vaultId, when scanNewLines runs, then it still blocks the line
Record a bounded git summary of the cwd and compare drift cwd-state.ts

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/cwd-state.ts per FR-12: readCwdState(cwd) uses promisified execFile git calls (remote get-url origin, rev-parse HEAD, branch --show-current, status --porcelain=v1) and returns { gitOrigin, head, branch, dirty, staged, unstaged, untracked, conflicted } counts, or null when cwd is not a git repo. compareCwdState(saved, current) returns the list of differing fields. No paths, diffs or file contents appear in the result. No execSync.

items.title: Given a temp git repo with one staged and one untracked file, when readCwdState runs, then it returns staged 1, untracked 1, dirty true, and no field contains a file path
Given a non-git temp dir, when readCwdState runs, then it returns null
Given saved and current states with different HEAD, when compareCwdState runs, then it returns ["head"]
Define the VaultStore interface, the dir backend and the shared contract suite

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/store/types.ts with the VaultStore interface from PRD "Backend interface" plus VaultOfflineError. Implement src/lib/vault/store/dir.ts over a local directory using the P-3 layout (VAULT-FORMAT marker, objects/<id[0:2]>/<id>, refs/<name>), with version = SHA-1 of the ref file bytes and casRef serialized by an O_EXCL lock file. Write the reusable suite tests/unit/lib/vault/store/contract.ts exporting runVaultStoreContract(makeStore) covering idempotent putObjects, getObject of a missing id, hasObjects, readRef/casRef/listRefs(prefix), and a CAS race where two concurrent casRef calls with the same expectedVersion yield exactly one "ok".

items.title: Given the dir backend, when runVaultStoreContract runs, then every case passes
Given two concurrent casRef calls with the same expectedVersion, when both settle, then exactly one returns "ok" and the other returns "conflict"
Given putObjects is called twice with the same id and bytes, then the second call succeeds and the object bytes are unchanged
Implement the git backend that passes the shared contract suite

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns only store/git.ts and its test; it shares no file with any other item and runs the contract suite created by store-contract.

narrative.Action: Implement src/lib/vault/store/git.ts per PRD decision P-4: local clone at vaultDir()/git, branch main, promisified execFile with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, putObjects writes files uncommitted, casRef = fetch, reset --hard origin/main, compare blob SHA, write, one commit, push; a non-fast-forward rejection repeats up to 3 times then returns "conflict"; a network failure resets to origin/main and throws VaultOfflineError. Also export initGitVault(url) (clone; refuse a non-empty remote without VAULT-FORMAT; write VAULT-FORMAT on an empty remote). On an empty remote there is no origin/main: skip fetch/reset, treat every ref as version null, and create main with git push -u origin main on the first casRef. Never git stash; never touch any repo other than the vault clone. Tests use a local bare repo fixture and two clones under separate temp OVERDECK_HOMEs.

items.title: Given a bare repo fixture, when runVaultStoreContract runs against the git backend, then every case passes including the CAS race across two clones
Given the remote is unreachable, when casRef runs, then it throws VaultOfflineError and the clone has no commit that origin/main lacks
Given a non-empty remote without VAULT-FORMAT, when initGitVault runs, then it refuses and makes no commit or push
Keep the machine-local index of owned tails and list cache local-index.ts

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/local-index.ts per PRD decision P-18: vaultDir()/index.json (0600, atomic), owned: map nativePath -> { vaultId, harness, tail }, and listCache: array of { vaultId, title, harness, ownerLabel, ownerIsHere, updatedAt, tombstone }. Provide getOwned, setOwnedTail, replaceListCache, readListCache. Nothing in this file is ever uploaded.

items.title: Given setOwnedTail runs for a path, when getOwned runs in a new process, then it returns the persisted tail
Given replaceListCache runs, when readListCache runs, then it returns the same rows in the same order
Given index.json is written, then its mode is 0600
Match exclusions by path, origin and session exclude.ts

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/exclude.ts per PRD decision P-11: isExcluded({ cwd, gitOrigin, nativeSessionId, vaultId }, config.exclude) returns true when cwd is under an exclude.paths entry (path-segment aware, so /a/b does not match /a/bc), gitOrigin equals an exclude.origins entry, or the session id or vaultId is in exclude.sessions. addExclusion/removeExclusion update config.json through config.ts.

items.title: Given exclude.paths ["/a/b"], when isExcluded runs for cwd "/a/b/c", then it returns true, and for cwd "/a/bc" it returns false
Given exclude.origins contains the repo origin, when isExcluded runs for a cwd in that repo, then it returns true
Given removeExclusion runs for an entry, when isExcluded runs again, then it returns false
Run one settlement: continuity, secret scan, chunks and record CAS settle.ts

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns only settle.ts and its test; every module it composes is delivered by its blocks predecessors.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/settle.ts per PRD "Settlement" and decisions P-5, P-6: settle({ nativePath, harness, store, keys }) returns { verdict: "noop"|"append"|"diverged"|"blocked"|"excluded"|"offline", vaultId, chunks }. It skips excluded sessions (vault-exclude), reads from tail.byteOffset, runs checkContinuity, scans new lines (vault-secrets; any hit returns "blocked" with the hits and writes nothing), splits into chunks, putObjects, appends a settlement entry with countHumanTurns and readCwdState, recomputes the VIEW on a compaction boundary (Claude line with "isCompactSummary":true; Codex {"type":"compacted"}; other harnesses VIEW = whole log), then casRef. First settlement mints vaultId and a segment owned by ensureEnvironmentIdentity(). If the record owner is not this machine, save the new lines as a fork record per P-6. On VaultOfflineError return "offline" and do not advance the local index. On "diverged" write nothing and return the verdict.

items.title: Given a new transcript, when settle runs twice with 2 new lines appended between runs, then the second run uploads only chunks for the 2 new lines
Given a transcript whose saved middle line changed, when settle runs, then it returns "diverged" and makes no putObjects or casRef call
Given a new line containing an API key, when settle runs, then it returns "blocked" with the line number and pattern and writes nothing

Given the record owner changed to another environmentId, when settle runs with new lines, then it creates a fork record owned here whose parent is the last settled version and leaves the original record unchanged
Given the store throws VaultOfflineError, when settle runs, then it returns "offline" and the local index tail is unchanged
Run the push/pull sync cycle with backoff and list refresh sync.ts

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/sync.ts: syncOnce() settles every owned native transcript in the local index whose size grew, upserts this machine ref m/<hmac(environmentId)> with { environmentId, label, lastSyncAt }, pulls all r/ refs, decrypts them, skips values whose type is not "session" (FR-9), and replaces the list cache. On VaultOfflineError it returns { offline: true } without throwing or logging per record. createSyncLoop({ intervalSec }) retries offline cycles with exponential backoff capped at intervalSec (used by PAN-4307; tested here with vi.useFakeTimers()).

items.title: Given machine A settled a transcript, when syncOnce runs on machine B, then B list cache contains the record with ownerLabel of A and ownerIsHere false
Given a ref whose decrypted type is "task", when syncOnce runs, then it skips that ref and completes without error
Given the store is offline, when createSyncLoop runs under fake timers, then retries occur at increasing delays capped at intervalSec and no error is thrown
Skip CLI telemetry and heartbeat for pan vault invocations

narrative.Action: Per PRD decision P-12: in src/cli/telemetry.ts, when the first positional argv (after node and script) is "vault", runCliWithTelemetry runs the command without constructing the analytics lifecycle and without maybeSendInstanceHeartbeat, so no PostHog client is created. Other verbs keep the current behavior.

items.title: Given argv ["vault","status"], when runCliWithTelemetry runs, then getAnalyticsService and maybeSendInstanceHeartbeat are never called
Given argv ["status"], when runCliWithTelemetry runs, then telemetry behaves exactly as before (lifecycle finish is called)
Register the pan vault group with setup, join and status verbs

expected_outputs: lint completes without errors including lint-skills
metadata.parallelSafeReason: The only CLI item with no CLI predecessor; later CLI items that share index.ts and SKILL.md are serialized after it by blocks edges.

narrative.Action: Per decisions P-1..P-4 and P-13: add registerVaultCommands(program) in src/cli/commands/vault/index.ts and a vault group in src/cli/command-groups.ts (names ["vault"]), each verb a lazyAction import. setup <git-url>: refuse if already enabled with a different backend, create the key, initGitVault, write h/header, ensureEnvironmentIdentity, write config backend, and print the 24-word phrase once with the warning "Anyone with these words can read your vault. Losing every device and these words loses the vault." join <git-url>: prompt for the phrase (or --phrase-file), verify via h/header, save key and config. status: print backend, machine label and environmentId, owned record count, last sync, and the machine list. With the vault off, status prints VAULT_OFF_MESSAGE and exits 0. Create sync-sources/skills/pan-vault/SKILL.md matching --help so scripts/lint-skills.sh passes. Check scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt if src/cli/index.ts grows.

items.title: Given an empty OVERDECK_HOME and a bare repo, when pan vault setup <url> runs, then it prints 24 words and the key-loss warning once and a second status run prints the backend and no phrase
Given a second OVERDECK_HOME, when pan vault join <url> runs with the correct phrase, then it saves the key and status lists both machines after sync
Given a wrong phrase, when pan vault join runs, then it prints "The recovery phrase does not match this vault." and writes no key file
Given no backend is configured, when pan vault status runs, then it prints the vault-off message and exits 0
Given npm run lint runs, then scripts/lint-skills.sh reports no drift for pan-vault
Add pan vault save and pan vault sync verbs including the Stop-hook mode

narrative.Action: Add save [session-id|path] with --all, --since <date>, --harness <h>, and --hook (P-15: read {session_id, transcript_path} JSON from stdin, never write stdout, always exit 0), resolving sessions through src/lib/conversations/harness-discovery.ts discovery roots. Print per session the verdict (appended N lines, noop, blocked at line N: pattern, diverged, excluded, offline). Add sync calling syncOnce and printing counts. With the vault off every verb prints VAULT_OFF_MESSAGE and exits 0 (save --hook prints nothing). Update SKILL.md.

items.title: Given three discovered Claude sessions with mtimes on different days, when pan vault save --all --since <date> runs, then it saves exactly the sessions modified on or after that date
Given the vault is off, when pan vault save --hook runs with hook JSON on stdin, then it writes nothing to stdout and exits 0
Given a session with a secret, when pan vault save <id> runs, then it prints "blocked at line N: <pattern>" and exits non-zero
Add pan vault list and pan vault show verbs with the owner badge

narrative.Action: Add list (reads the list cache only, never the backend; columns vaultId prefix, title, harness, owner label marked "(this machine)" when ownerIsHere, updatedAt; --json) and show <id> (fetches and decrypts the record and its chunks and prints the human turns and assistant text read-only, plus settlements with version numbers for @version). Update SKILL.md.

items.title: Given the list cache holds a record owned by machine A, when pan vault list runs on machine B, then it prints the title with owner label A and without "(this machine)"
Given a record with 3 settlements, when pan vault show <id> runs, then it prints the conversation text and lists versions 1..3
Given the backend is unreachable, when pan vault list runs, then it prints the cached rows and exits 0
Materialize a Claude Code session from the VIEW and restore native files materialize.ts

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns only materialize.ts and its test until codex-resume-checkpoint, which is serialized after it.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/materialize.ts per PRD "Materialization" and P-5: materializeClaude({ record, store, keys, targetCwd, newSessionId }) fetches and decrypts the VIEW chunks and writes ~/.claude/projects/<slug(targetCwd)>/<newSessionId>.jsonl, rewriting only each line's "sessionId":"<old>" and (if the cwd changed) "cwd":"<old>" substrings by exact string replacement so all other bytes are unchanged; it refuses to overwrite an existing file. Compute the directory with claudeProjectDir(targetCwd) (encodeClaudeProjectDir, src/lib/runtimes/storage/claude-code.ts line 37); never import a slug helper from src/lib/overdeck/*, which the import guard bans. restoreNative({ record, nativePath }) rebuilds a native file of this machine's current segment byte-for-byte (the adopter prefix is re-materialized deterministically from segment.prefix, then the segment's own LOG lines follow).

items.title: Given a record with a compaction boundary, when materializeClaude runs, then the written file starts at the boundary line and every line differs from the saved line only in the sessionId value
Given a saved original-owner transcript, when restoreNative runs after the file is removed, then the rebuilt file is byte-identical to the original
Given an adopted segment, when restoreNative runs, then the rebuilt file is byte-identical to the adopter file as settled
Given the target file already exists, when materializeClaude runs, then it refuses and leaves the file unchanged
Transfer ownership by CAS and fork at a version adopt.ts

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns only adopt.ts and its test.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/vault/adopt.ts per decisions P-5 and P-7: adoptRecord({ vaultId, targetCwd }) reads the record, refuses when the owner is this machine, appends a lineage entry and a new segment (prefix describing the VIEW range, sessionIdFrom/To, cwdFrom/To), casRefs it, and only on "ok" calls materializeClaude; on "conflict" it re-reads and returns { alreadyContinuedOn: <label> } without writing any native file. forkRecordAtVersion({ vaultId, version }) creates a new record (new vaultId, owned here) whose log is the parent chunk ids through settlement n and whose parent is { vaultId, version: n }; the original ref is never written. The origin machine native file is never touched.
